decisions.quote: Acharya and Pedersen (2005) study the effect of liquidity risk on the cross-section of asset returns and develop the LCAPM formula with the four testable hypotheses that (1) the intercept term is zero, (2) the illiquidity costs have a positive effect, (3) the net liquidity risk also has a positive effect, and (4) the market risk premium is equal to the liquidity risk premium. This paper tests the validity of the AP LCAPM for six models, eight test portfolios, and three different datasets (the 1964 to 1999 US data, the recent 2000-16 US data, and the 1978-2012 Japanese data).
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind target identify Acharya and Pedersen (2005), 'Asset Pricing with Liquidity Risk,' as the original study being re-tested, and the shipped record provides its valid DOI.

decisions.location: Section 1 Introduction (Main Findings of Our Paper), p. 80, lines 332-335
decisions.quote:
In summary, from the above results (and also from Holden and Nam (2018)),
although we observe improvements in a fit of the AP LCAPM over the CAPM
in terms of R2 , one has to conclude that the LCAPM does not satisfy either of
the one-variable LCAPM test and the two-variable LCAPM test.
decisions.reason: The paper conducts a hybrid empirical workflow: (1) an original-period re-analysis of US 1964-1999 observations reconstructed from the same CRSP, COMPUSTAT, and French databases where exact coefficient recovery ('quantitative replication') was abandoned due to incomplete original documentation, passing 7/16 one-variable and 3/24 two-variable tests (vs. Acharya & Pedersen's 8/16 and 1/24), and (2) out-of-sample replications on later US 2000-2016 (8/16 and 1/24) and Japanese 1978-2012 (0/16 and 0/24) samples. The headline pass percentages (36.0% and 5.2%) pool AP's own reported regressions with the three datasets, and the summary negative conclusion combines the original-period and new-sample tests alongside Holden and Nam (2018). Because the record-level study type is genuinely hybrid and unresolved between reproduction and replication, and the codebook requires different outcome schemas for each without transferring a pooled count or substituting a categorical replication label for reproduction axes, outcome is undeterminable.

decisions.quote:
Our first interest is the “quantitative replication” that the estimated coefficients
must be equal to the original AP estimates (with possible small differences). But
the AP paper does not provide full details of the estimation procedure. Therefore,
it is objectively not possible to determine the exact estimation procedure employed
by AP from the paper.4 Under such circumstances, it is not feasible to adopt the
“quantitative replication” criterion to evaluate a replication attempt of AP.
decisions.reason: The paper combines two distinct empirical designs targeting Acharya and Pedersen (2005) in a single study: (1) an original-period re-analysis of US 1964-1999 observations reconstructed from the same CRSP, COMPUSTAT, and Kenneth French sources (Section 2.1, p. 80), where exact coefficient recovery was abandoned as infeasible due to incomplete documentation of AP's estimation procedure, and (2) two out-of-sample replications using new datasets (US 2000-2016 and Japan 1978-2012). Independently downloading the same 1964-1999 market observations from the same databases does not make the original-period test different data, yet the new-sample tests are genuine replications. Because the codebook requires a single mutually exclusive record-level type ('reproduction' vs. 'replication') that determines whether dual reproduction axes or a single replication outcome apply, and neither workflow can be dropped without distorting the paper's primary scope, record-level type is undeterminable.

parent_review.parent_objection: The paper explicitly reconstructs the original-period US observations and defines quantitative recovery of original coefficients as one research question,then adds later-US and Japanese samples. The primary hybrid workflow and dependent outcome are unsettled after parent source inspection. Two Argon calls were already used(including one mechanical retry),so no final scope call is available and no third call is made. Original identity is retained separately.
